subject: Security exhibit: evidence ownership, pen-test access & comms cadence
messages:
From: Michael Soto <msoto@atlashealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyanka Roy <proy@atlashealth.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Security exhibit questions + proposed evidence cadence

Hi Camila,

Thanks for the updated MSA and order form. Our security team reviewed the security exhibit and has a few outstanding asks before we can move to signature. High-level: SOC 2 reporting cadence, explicit pen-test access language (including contractor access and SCADA adjacency controls), and clarity on evidence ownership for demo/poC artifacts.

We attached a short redline (atlas-security-exhibit-redlines.docx) with inline comments. Specific asks:
- SOC 2: we need confirmation on Type II report timing and whether Redwood will provide user-entity controls mapping.
- Pen test: request for a 30-day notice window for external vendors + scope exclusion list handling.
- Evidence cadence: recommend quarterly snapshot exports for critical logs (30/90/365 retention tiers) and a monthly status digest to our security inbox.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide: (a) a SOC 2 Type II report within 30 days of completion, (b) a temporary read-only S3 export of logs for audit windows, and (c) a defined process for granting pen-test access to our third-party vendor?

Appreciate a quick turnaround; procurement is waiting on the updated exhibit to finalize PO.

Best,
Michael Soto
Sr. InfoSec Manager
Atlas Health

Attachments: atlas-security-exhibit-redlines.docx (docx)

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Michael Soto <msoto@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit questions + proposed evidence cadence

Hi Michael — thanks for the redlines and helpful notes. Looping in Laura from Legal and Karthik who is supporting procurement so we can align on commercial timing.

Quick answers up front:
1) SOC 2 Type II: Redwood will provide the latest SOC 2 Type II report (when completed) and can commit to delivering it to your security mailbox within 30 days of issuance. We will also share a UEC (User-Entity Controls) mapping doc as a supplement where applicable.
2) Pen test access: we can accommodate a vendor-led pen test during a pre-agreed window. Proposed process:
   - Customer submits pen-test request with vendor details 30 days prior
   - Redwood security reviews and provides a scoped approval or suggested exclusions within 5 business days
   - Access is provisioned to a dedicated test deployment or restricted environment; production access is not granted without additional approval and a signed addendum
3) Evidence exports: we can provide periodic exports (S3 or secure Drive) and a monthly digest; retention tiers are configurable via the order form addendum.

Laura, can you review the redline attached and propose language for the pen-test access flow and evidence ownership (we think the right model is Redwood retains system-level logs; customers can request exported snapshots for audit). Karthik — if we agree this week, can we update the order form and get procurement a PO timeline?

Thanks — I attached a draft pen-test schedule spreadsheet (proposed-pen-test-window.xlsx) and will circulate a short playbook for evidence requests.

Cheers,
Camila Reyes
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-pen-test-window.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit questions + proposed evidence cadence

Camila / Karthik — I reviewed Atlas's redlines. Two points for internal alignment before we send proposed language:

1) Pen-test clause: Atlas asks for contractor access language. We should offer a standard "authorized third-party testing" flow that includes: vendor scoping, limited test window, no production account takeover, and obligation for Atlas to provide proof of authorization for the vendor. We'll add a clause that Redwood may require mitigation steps before granting any elevated interaction. Suggested short clause to propose: "Customer may engage an authorized third-party security assessor to perform a penetration test of Redwood services in a pre-approved scope and window. Customer must provide 30 days' advance notice and evidence of assessor credentials; Redwood reserves the right to restrict scope for safety and to require remediation acceptance before production changes."

2) Evidence ownership & export: Atlas is requesting regular exports for audit. We need to be careful about where responsibility sits for PII/regulated data in those exports. I propose: Redwood retains system and infrastructure logs as system records; Redwood will provide, on request, exported snapshots of customer-specific telemetry/logs for the agreed audit period, subject to a Data Export Addendum (DEA) that includes a transfer security checklist. That addendum will define export format, retention expectations, and a delivery SLA (we can propose 10 business days for standard requests, shorter for scheduled snapshots).

I attached a short playbook (evidence-cadence-playbook.pdf) with suggested SLA language and an example UEC mapping snippet we can share with the customer.

Once you confirm, I will draft redline text for the exhibit and the standalone DEA. Karthik — please confirm commercial runway for including a DEA in the order form (e.g., standard 90d review).

-Laura
Associate General Counsel
Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence-cadence-playbook.pdf (pdf)

From: Priyanka Roy <proy@atlashealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Michael Soto <msoto@atlashealth.com>
Cc: External Auditor <audit@thirdpartyaudit.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Security exhibit questions + proposed evidence cadence

Thanks Camila/Laura — a couple clarifying points from procurement/security: 
- The auditor needs the UEC mapping as soon as possible; can you share a template view or a redacted example?
- For exports: does Redwood support SFTP and encrypted S3 exports? Our compliance team prefers S3 with customer-managed keys.
- Pen-test: the vendor requires at least a 14-day window on your side for pre-test coordination.

Is it possible to get the DEA draft and the UEC example by end of week? That will help us keep the PO on the current timeline.

Thanks,
Priyanka Roy
Sr. Procurement Manager
Atlas Health

Hi Priyanka / Michael — thanks for the quick turnaround. Laura and I reviewed and attached two artifacts: the security exhibit redline with proposed language and a Data Export Addendum (DEA) draft. Summary of the proposed positions: 

- SOC 2: Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II report within 30 days of issuance and a UEC mapping (redacted example included). We can deliver the UEC mapping to your auditor under NDA.
- Pen test: Proposed exhibit language matches Laura's suggestion. We accept a 30-day notice for vendor-led tests; Redwood requires vendor credentials and restricts some infrastructure-specific subsystems. We will coordinate a dedicated staging/test harness for high-risk tests.
- Evidence exports: Redwood supports S3 exports with customer-managed keys (CMKs) and SFTP if required. The DEA sets a 10 business day SLA for scheduled snapshots and 15 business days for ad-hoc exports; emergency exports may be negotiated.

Next steps / action items:
1) Atlas: confirm acceptance of the DEA and the proposed pen-test clause by EOD Friday 2027-04-16.
2) Redwood: Laura will update the exhibit and DEA redlines and deliver final documents for signature once Atlas confirms.
3) Audit access: if Atlas wants the auditor (audit@thirdpartyaudit.com) to receive the UEC mapping directly, please confirm and provide an NDA signed by the auditor.

I've attached: atlas-security-exhibit-redlines.docx (with our edits), evidence-cadence-playbook.pdf, and DEA-draft.docx. If that works, Karthik will update the order form with the DEA as an addendum and we can route the package to procurement.

Thanks all — happy to hop on a short call if you want to walk the language.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Lead, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
